For device-factor-single-otp-m03, the received object is otpCode. The corrected browser-receive wording preserves user input and Realm A provider ownership without claiming successful OTP validation.

For device-factor-single-passkey-m03, this named m03 operation still receives otpCode in the browser; the variant identifier does not turn this operation into a passkey proof. Realm A owns the OTP form.

For device-factor-single-web-m03, the originally reported key now names the Realm A identity provider as form owner. Browser receipt from Person is retained, with no transfer to the separate confidential requesting application.

For device-factor-single-web-otp-m03, browser receipt and OTP data are explicit. The provider form is Realm A even when the requesting device is a web backend; no application-owned OTP form is implied.

For device-factor-single-web-passkey-m03, current context identifies browser/otpCode/receive. The complete message respects that actual operation and names the Realm A provider form, not an inferred passkey operation or requesting application.
For single-m03, browser receives the displayed code entered by Person. The single-realm producer maps provider B to Realm A, and the corrected Native names that provider, not app.
For single-otp-m03, receipt of the typed OTP in the browser is preserved. Realm A is the identity-provider form owner, and receiving the code does not itself establish authentication.
For single-passkey-m03, the actual member is an OTP receive operation despite its scenario identifier. The corrected text retains that role and the Realm A provider boundary.
For single-web-m03, browser receives Person-entered code for the Realm A provider form. Web-application architecture does not make the application the form owner.
For single-web-otp-m03, corrected complete wording describes browser receipt of OTP at the Realm A identity-provider form. It does not forward the seed or claim acceptance of the factor.
For single-web-passkey-m03, actual browser/otpCode/receive governs the prose. The new provider-owner wording is correct independently of the variant name, and no factor-validation verdict is added.
